claims.text: Increasing Al content in CrFeCoNiAl high-entropy alloys promotes diffusion of Al from the bulk to the surface.
Enhanced surface diffusion of Al promotes preferential formation of an Al2O3 scale.
The oxide formed by the modified alloy will specifically be α-Al2O3.
The α-Al2O3 scale will be coherent, dense, adherent, continuous, and slow-growing.
The protective α-Al2O3 scale will form and persist on CrFeCoNiAl above 900 °C.
A coherent alumina scale minimizes interfacial strain and prevents stress accumulation.
Minimizing interfacial strain and stress accumulation reduces oxide cracking and spallation.
Increasing Al content increases the thermodynamic or chemical driving force for Al diffusion to the surface.
Alloying strategies used in TiAl alloys provide an analogue for promoting continuous alumina formation in CrFeCoNiAl alloys.
Lower or non-optimized-Al CrFeCoNiX baseline alloys typically form unstable oxide scales prone to cracking and spallation.
Compared with the lower-Al baseline, the higher-Al alloy will form a more continuous and adherent α-Al2O3 scale with less cracking and spallation.
The higher-Al alloy will exhibit lower oxide growth or weight-gain kinetics than the baseline alloy.
Internal oxidation can embrittle the substrate and contribute to scale spallation.
Si, Mn, and the presence of multiple metallic phases may alter Al diffusion kinetics and oxide adherence.

contradictions.description: The central hypothesis is restricted to X = Al and proposes increasing Al, whereas the boundary also claims coverage of X = Si or Mn without defining whether Al is added to those alloys, substituted for X, or absent. Thus the intervention and composition scope are not consistently defined.

The outcome predicts a defect-free, stable α-Al2O3 layer, while the hypothesis explicitly leaves the required Al threshold, phase effects, and effects of Si or Mn unresolved. This makes the categorical 'defect-free' prediction stronger than the stated uncertainty supports.
